project_name: O'Neil Digital Solutions Monroe printing and data center
aliases: O'Neil Digital Solutions Union County project
status_detail: 2015 local reporting described a $140 million printing and data center project in Monroe creating 250 jobs, with Union County and Monroe incentives. Monroe City Council minutes later described the county's industrial base as diversified by adding digital printing/data center and listed O'Neil Digital Solutions among significant locations/expansions. Monroe economic development site references ongoing O'Neil Digital Solutions investment incentive activity.
notes: This appears to be an enterprise/digital-printing/data-services facility rather than a hyperscale colocation campus; kept because original local economic-development records call it a data center project.

aliases: Vance County US-158 Business data center
developer: Natelli Holdings LLC; Natelli Investments LLC
status_detail: Vance County commissioners approved a contested rezoning in April 2026 for Natelli-linked land along US-158 Business near Pine Meadow Trail/Horseshoe Bend Road. Data Center Dynamics and WRAL reported the rezoning could support a data center, while a July 2026 WIZS interview with a Vance commissioner said no formal data-center application had yet been made to the county.
notes: Kept as a planned/early-stage lead because the approved rezoning is real but project specifics and end user remain unconfirmed. Citizen report says ZMA26-001 was about 40 acres, while later local summaries discuss about 113 acres across multiple parcels.

status_detail: Developer project site described a proposed campus west of I-540 between US-1 and Old US-1 with four 200,000-square-foot data-center buildings near Shearon Harris Nuclear Plant and the Western Wake Regional Water Reclamation Facility. WUNC reported on March 5, 2026 that the developer withdrew annexation and rezoning applications for the proposed 300 MW facility while Apex considered zoning changes; WRAL earlier described the proposal as 250 MW on about 190 acres.
notes: Capacity reports vary between 250 MW and 300 MW; used WUNC's 300 MW for the withdrawn proposal and noted WRAL's 250 MW report.
